records.stem: ww Which of the following is NOT a typical cause of a bitemporal hemianopia:
options: Optic glioma (Vv) Posterior cerebral artery stroke 78%
Aneurysm of the anterior communicating artery
records.explanation: A bitemporal hemianopia is most likely due to compression at the optic chiasm. This may be caused by pituitary tumour, craniopharyngioma, meningioma, optic glioma or aneurysm of the internal carotid artery. records.stem: ww Occlusion of which of the following blood vessels is most likely to result in a receptive dysphasia:
records.explanation: The middle cerebral artery supplies the lateral convexity of the cerebral hemisphere including a large proportion of the frontal lobe, temporal lobe and parietal lobe. Receptive dysphasia is caused by damage to the Wernicke's speech area in the dominant superior temporal lobe which is supplied by the middle cerebral artery. : v Arterial Supply of Brain

records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: A 29 year old male racing driver has fractured a cervical vertebra. On examination, he has weakness of the right side of his body with upgoing plantars, loss of pain and temperature sensation in his left limbs, with normal fine-touch sensation over all four limbs. This clinical picture is most likely seen in a lesion of the:
options: Anterior column, left side (x) Anterior column, right side 19% (Vv) Lateral column, right side 46%
records.explanation: The lesion is likely affecting the corticospinal and lateral spinothalamic tracts in the lateral column. Motor power of the limbs is mediated by the ipsilateral corticospinal tract, and pain and temperature sensation is mediated by the contralateral spinothalamic tract, therefore the lesion is likely on the right side. The posterior column is spared, as fine-touch sensation is normal throughout. v Spinal Cord Tracts
